newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on long liquidation.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended down from the previous New York close on long liquidation after a strong rally in New York on Friday proved a damp squib on Monday in Asian time zones, bullion dealers said.
"I think the market got too bullish on the (Hong Kong) open because of the strong (New York Friday) close and the longs got out," said a dealer at an international bank.
Bullion ended at US$362.20/70 an ounce Monday against New York's US$363.00/50 close on Friday.
Punters around the world saw the spurt in New York prices just before the Friday close, noted good buying activity on Saturday and got long, dealers said.
"Everyone was waiting to make what was going to be a nice easy quick buck on the Monday morning open, I was sucked in as well, I thought it would jump another dollar," one dealer said.

Market sentiment was mixed following the rally's fadeout and support was seen at $362 per ounce, although some dealers felt that without the long liquidation, gold would have held at $362.50 per ounce.
Local gold ended HK$11 lower at HK$3,354 a tael.
The carry over charge per 10 taels of gold at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose slightly to +5.00 from +4.00 at its previous fix.
